description: Hardware-agnostic machine learning infrastructure for .NET. Implements high-performance neural network layers in C# that transpile to WebGPU, CUDA, OpenCL, and WebGL via SpawnDev.ILGPU. Optimized for Blazor WebAssembly and native GPU execution.
releaseNotes: v5.2.4 - FIX: a REVERSED slice - x[..., ::-1] - produced an ALL-ZEROS buffer on every backend. SliceOperator.Execute clamped `ends` into [0, dim] whatever the sign of the step; ONNX clamps it into [-1, dim-1] for a negative step, because a reversed slice legitimately ends one BEFORE index 0 - which is exactly what the INT64_MIN sentinel torch emits for ::-1 means. Floored at 0, both copy loops ran for (i = 2; i < 0; i += -1): zero iterations, output buffer never written, no exception. What hid it: the SHAPE was already correct, because GraphCompiler and the shape interpreter both handled negative steps - so the tensor had exactly the dimensions ONNX specifies and was full of zeros, every downstream shape check passed, and the model just returned a wrong number. Any model using a reversed slice was affected. Found by running Silero VAD against onnxruntime, whose adaptive_normalization reverses a [1,1,3] axis twice. Blast radius audited with a new tool rather than assumed. Gated by 9 cases (6 reversed, 3 forward) on all six backends. ADDED: Silero VAD on our engine, matching onnxruntime to 3.3e-8 on the speech probability and 1.1e-6 on the LSTM state over 125 frames of real speech, with the state threaded frame to frame - plus a FROZEN-STATE negative control in the fixture, because an engine caching h/c would otherwise pass wherever the two happened to agree. ADDED: VoiceActivityDetector + SileroVad - streaming endpointing that turns microphone samples into finished utterances, accepting any chunk size and reframing to the model's fixed 512 internally. Follows silero-vad's own VADIterator including the negative-threshold hysteresis, with the defaults RoseEars runs on the robot (0.5 threshold, 500ms min-silence, 250ms min-speech, 20s max-speech). Gated against sherpa-onnx - a separate implementation of the same endpointing - at 3/3 segments, worst boundary 14 ms. PERFORMANCE: the LSTM recurrence moved onto the accelerator. LSTMOperator computed on the HOST - it read X, initial_h and initial_c back, ran the recurrence in C#, and uploaded Y/Y_h/Y_c, which is fine where a readback is a synchronous memcpy and is not fine in a browser, where each one is a mapAsync that flushes the command encoder and WAITS. New Kernels/RecurrentKernels runs it on the GPU (gather-only, one thread per (batch, hidden) unit, time loop outside the kernel - a persistent single-workgroup RNN cannot run on WebGL). The executor's readback skip-set was sharpened to match: it is now per INPUT POSITION rather than per op (Squeeze(data, axes) needs a value for AXES and never reads DATA), and the value-needing set is computed backwards to a FIXED POINT so an op like Concat - whose inputs are all data - needs their values only when something downstream reads its own output. MEASURED per frame on Silero VAD (a frame is 32 ms of audio): WebGPU 177.9 -> 98.7 ms with readbacks 16 -> 5, WebGL 85.6 -> 60.3 ms, Wasm 191.8 -> 162.4 ms, and on OpenCL the p99 collapsed from 47.4 ms to 7.78 ms - which matters more than the mean, since a 47 ms spike against a 32 ms budget is a frame you cannot catch up from. Any repeat-inference browser workload whose frame time is dominated by small mid-graph readbacks should benefit. GRU and RNN still take the host path. Full six-backend sweep green. See Changelog.
